data.explanation: Institute suggested answer: A. Production volume ratio = Standard hours for actual output ÷ Budgeted/available hours × 100, using the hours after excluding the stated idle time as prescribed.

data.q: Hotel Dream House is having 250 rooms of which 70% are normally occupied in summer and 40% are occupied in winter. Period of summer and winter be taken as 6 months each and normal days in a month be assumed to be 30. What is the value of total occupied room days?
data.explanation: Institute suggested answer: D. Summer occupied room-days = 250 × 70% × 6 × 30 = 31,500. Winter occupied room-days = 250 × 40% × 6 × 30 = 18,000. Total = 49,500 room-days, which is option D.

data.q: A Lorry starts with a load of 40 Metric Tonnes (MT) of goods from Station A. It unloads 16 MT in Station B and the balance goods in Station C. On return trip, it reaches Station A with a load of 32 MT, loaded at Station C. The distance between A to B, B to C and C to A are 40 kms, 60 kms and 80 kms respectively. On the basis of above information, Commercial MT-kilometers are —
data.explanation: Institute suggested answer: B. Commercial tonne-kilometres are calculated using the commercial load carried on each leg. Multiply each leg's load by its distance and add the outward and return movements; the institute key gives 5,760 MT-km.

data.q: In a process 800 units are introduced during 2023-24. 5% of input is normal loss. Closing work-in-progress 60% complete is 100 units. 660 completed units are transferred to next process. Equivalent production for the period is
data.explanation: Institute suggested answer: D. First determine normal loss (5% of 800 = 40 units), then account for completed units and the 60%-complete closing WIP to calculate equivalent units.

data.q: Following information is available: Opening stock = 4,000; Closing stock = 6,400; Material consumed = 31,200. On the above basis, what is the Inventory Turnover Ratio?
data.explanation: Institute suggested answer: C. Average inventory = (Opening stock + Closing stock) ÷ 2 = (4,000 + 6,400) ÷ 2 = 5,200. Inventory turnover = 31,200 ÷ 5,200 = 6 times.

data.q: When P/V ratio is 20% and margin of safety ratio is 30%, profit is of sales.
data.explanation: Institute suggested answer: B. Profit as a percentage of sales = Margin of Safety ratio × P/V ratio. With 20% MOS and 60% P/V ratio, profit = 20% × 60% = 12% of sales.

data.q: In P Ltd., labour force at the beginning of July 2023 was 3,800 and at the end of July 2023 was 4,200. During the month, 50 workers left while 80 workers were discharged. 560 workers were engaged out of which only 60 were appointed in the vacancy created by the number of workers separated and the rest on account of expansion scheme. On the basis of above information, Labour Turnover Ratio of the firm by Flux Method is
data.explanation: Institute suggested answer: D. Under the Flux method, labour turnover = (Separations + Accessions) ÷ Average workforce × 100. Use the workers who left/discharged and the workers engaged with the stated basis, then divide by average workforce.

data.q: A company requires 1,00,000 units of an item annually. The cost per unit is ₹10. Ordering cost is ₹500 per order and inventory carrying cost is 50% per unit per annum. The Economic Order Quantity (EOQ) in this case is
data.explanation: Institute suggested answer: B. EOQ = √(2 × Annual demand × Ordering cost ÷ Annual carrying cost per unit). Using the figures given gives approximately 4,472 units.

data.q: In the year 2023-24, X & Co. used 2,820 kg of material at a total standard cost of ₹11,562. The material usage variance was ₹123 (Favourable). In the above case, Standard Weight of Material (SQ) for the period is

data.q: The main purpose of management accounting is to support management in planning, control and decision-making.
data.explanation: Management accounting supplies information for internal planning, control and decisions.

data.q: A cost object is best described as an item for which cost is measured.
data.explanation: A cost object may be a product, service, customer, job or other item whose cost is measured.

data.q: Maintenance of a common factory building is generally a facility-level activity.
data.explanation: Facility-level activities support the organisation or facility as a whole.

data.q: If fixed cost is ₹30,000, desired profit ₹15,000 and P/V ratio 30%, required sales are:
data.explanation: Required sales = (Fixed cost + desired profit) / P/V ratio = ₹45,000 / 30% = ₹1,50,000.

data.q: If selling price falls while variable cost and fixed cost remain unchanged, the break-even sales value will generally:
data.explanation: A lower contribution per unit reduces the P/V ratio, so more sales are needed to cover fixed cost.

data.q: Under ABC, a machine setup is normally treated as a:
data.explanation: A setup is performed for a batch, so setup costs are normally batch-level.

data.q: A cost driver is the factor that causes or influences the cost of an activity.
data.explanation: The cost driver explains the consumption of an activity and is used to assign activity costs.

data.q: A decision to discontinue a product should consider the contribution lost and avoidable fixed costs.
data.explanation: Relevant analysis focuses on future costs and benefits that differ between alternatives.

data.q: In standard costing, a variance is the difference between standard and actual performance.
data.explanation: Variance analysis compares actual results with predetermined standards.

data.q: The sales budget is normally the starting point for many operating budgets.
data.explanation: Expected sales drive production and many related operating budgets.

data.q: A flexible budget changes with the level of activity.
data.explanation: A flexible budget adjusts budgeted costs or revenues for the actual activity level.

data.q: Responsibility accounting assigns responsibility for controllable items to managers.
data.explanation: Responsibility accounting evaluates managers against items they can influence.

data.q: Under uncertainty, decision probabilities are not known with sufficient certainty.
data.explanation: Risk involves known or estimable probabilities; uncertainty does not.

data.q: Expected monetary value is calculated by multiplying each possible payoff by its probability and summing the results.
data.explanation: EMV is the probability-weighted average payoff.

data.q: A performance measure designed to connect operational activity with strategic objectives is commonly called a KPI.
data.explanation: Key Performance Indicators track important measures of organisational performance.

data.q: Management accounting is primarily concerned with information for internal management use.
data.explanation: Management accounting is an internal information function supporting managerial decisions.

data.q: Creation of value through effective use of resources is associated with the later, value-focused development of management accounting.
data.explanation: Modern management accounting increasingly emphasises value creation and strategic support.

data.q: The personnel who primarily use management accounting information for operational decisions are:
data.explanation: Managers use internal accounting information for planning, control and decisions.

data.q: Designing products is generally a product-level activity in an ABC framework.
data.explanation: Product design supports a product line rather than every individual unit or batch.

data.q: For fixed cost ₹10,000, variable cost ₹30,000 and sales ₹50,000, the P/V ratio is:
If sales are ₹50,000, variable cost ₹30,000 and fixed cost ₹10,000, profit is:
data.explanation: Contribution is ₹20,000 and profit = ₹20,000 − ₹10,000 = ₹10,000.

data.q: A make-or-buy decision should normally include the purchase price as a relevant cost of buying.
data.explanation: The purchase price changes between the alternatives and is therefore relevant.

data.q: A sunk cost is a past cost that cannot be changed by a current decision.
data.explanation: Sunk costs do not differ between current alternatives and are normally irrelevant.

data.q: Opportunity cost represents the benefit forgone by choosing one alternative instead of the next best alternative.
data.explanation: Opportunity cost measures the benefit sacrificed by an alternative choice.

data.q: A cash budget is prepared to forecast future cash receipts and payments.
data.explanation: Cash budgeting helps anticipate cash surpluses and shortages.

data.q: A standard cost is a predetermined cost established for a product or activity under specified conditions.
data.explanation: Standards are predetermined benchmarks used for control and variance analysis.

data.q: An adverse variance occurs when actual performance is less favourable than the standard or budget.
data.explanation: An adverse variance indicates an unfavourable deviation from the benchmark.

data.q: A profit centre manager is normally responsible for both revenues and costs of the centre.
data.explanation: A profit centre is evaluated on profit, so both revenues and controllable costs matter.

data.q: If fixed cost is ₹15,000, desired profit ₹5,000 and contribution per unit ₹4, required units are:
data.explanation: Required units = (₹15,000 + ₹5,000) / ₹4 = 5,000 units.

data.q: Minimum expected opportunity loss is obtained by choosing the decision with the lowest expected regret.
data.explanation: EOL is expected regret; the minimum EOL criterion selects the lowest expected regret.

data.q: A major role of management accounting is performance evaluation and variance analysis.
data.explanation: Management accounting supports performance measurement, control and analysis.

data.q: Activity-based costing is particularly useful when products consume overhead activities in different proportions.
data.explanation: ABC improves cost assignment where products use activities differently.

data.q: In ABC, some manufacturing costs may be excluded from product cost when they are not causally attributable under the selected design.
data.explanation: ABC does not automatically require every overhead item to be assigned to products.

data.q: If fixed cost is ₹10,000, variable cost ₹30,000 and sales ₹50,000, the P/V ratio is:
If P/V ratio is 45%, fixed cost ₹5,85,000 and margin of safety ratio 33⅓%, profit is:
data.explanation: At MOS ratio of 33⅓%, BE sales are two-thirds of actual sales. Using fixed cost/PV gives BE sales ₹13,00,000 and actual sales ₹19,50,000; MOS ₹6,50,000 and profit at 45% = ₹2,92,500.

data.q: A contribution margin is sales minus variable cost.
data.explanation: Contribution is the amount available to cover fixed costs and profit.

data.q: A higher P/V ratio, with fixed costs unchanged, generally reduces the break-even sales value.
data.explanation: Higher contribution per rupee of sales means fixed costs are recovered at a lower sales level.

data.q: For a limiting factor decision, products are commonly ranked using contribution per unit of the limiting factor.
data.explanation: The scarce resource should be allocated toward the highest contribution generated per unit of the constraint.

data.q: A special-order decision should compare incremental revenue with incremental and opportunity costs.
data.explanation: Only costs and revenues that change because of the special order are relevant, plus opportunity cost where applicable.

data.q: A transfer price is the price charged for goods or services transferred between responsibility centres.
data.explanation: Transfer pricing governs internal transfers between divisions or units.

data.q: A material price variance arises from a difference between actual and standard material price.
data.explanation: Price variance isolates the effect of paying a different material price from standard.

data.q: A production budget normally converts expected sales and desired inventory changes into planned production.
data.explanation: Production units are based on sales requirements plus desired closing inventory less opening inventory.

data.q: A master budget is a comprehensive summary of functional budgets.
data.explanation: The master budget consolidates the organisation's operating and financial plans.

data.q: A residual income measure charges a notional return on investment capital before assessing divisional performance.
data.explanation: Residual income is profit less a capital charge based on the required return.

data.q: Under risk, decision alternatives can be evaluated using probabilities of possible outcomes.
data.explanation: Risk differs from uncertainty because probabilities of outcomes can be assigned or estimated.

data.q: Management accounting is generally forward-looking and decision-oriented rather than limited to historical reporting.
data.explanation: Management accounting uses historical information but is primarily designed to support future decisions.

data.q: The break-even point is the level at which total revenue equals total cost.
data.explanation: At break-even, profit is zero because contribution exactly covers fixed costs.

data.q: Variance analysis helps management investigate the causes of deviations from standards or budgets.
data.explanation: Variance analysis identifies deviations and supports corrective action.

data.q: For a short-run make-or-buy decision, an unavoidable general fixed cost is normally:
data.explanation: If the fixed cost will remain regardless of the decision, it does not change between alternatives.

data.q: If sales are ₹9,00,000 and margin of safety is 40%, break-even sales are:
data.explanation: Margin of safety = Actual sales − BE sales. BE sales = 60% × ₹9,00,000 = ₹5,40,000.

data.q: Standard cost is best described as a predetermined benchmark cost.
data.explanation: Standard costs are established in advance for control and comparison.

data.q: The sales budget is generally prepared before the production budget.
data.explanation: Expected sales provide the basis for planning production.

data.q: Labour turnover measures the rate of change in the workforce.
data.explanation: Labour turnover indicates employee movement into and out of the organisation.

data.q: In a semi-variable cost, the fixed portion remains constant within a relevant range while the variable portion changes with activity.
data.explanation: Semi-variable costs contain both fixed and variable components.

data.q: Job costing is commonly used where individual jobs or units are separately identifiable.
data.explanation: Job costing accumulates costs for distinct jobs or orders.

data.q: A favourable material price variance means the actual material price is lower than the standard price, assuming the quantity is relevant.
data.explanation: Price variance compares actual price with standard price for actual quantity.

data.q: A cash budget may show a deficit even when an accounting profit is expected.
data.explanation: Profit and cash flow differ because of credit sales, non-cash items and timing of receipts/payments.

data.q: In responsibility accounting, managers should generally be evaluated on controllable items.
data.explanation: Controllability is central to fair managerial performance evaluation.

data.q: A decision tree is useful for decisions involving sequential choices and uncertain outcomes.
data.explanation: Decision trees map alternatives, chance events and resulting payoffs.

data.q: A KPI is a measurable indicator used to monitor an important aspect of performance.
data.explanation: KPIs track critical performance dimensions against targets.

data.q: Management accounting can be viewed as the study and application of accounting information for managerial purposes.
data.explanation: Management accounting focuses accounting information on management planning, control and decisions.

data.q: The ABC allocation sequence is activities, activity costs, cost drivers and then assignment to cost objects.
options: Activities → activity costs → cost drivers → cost objects
data.explanation: ABC first identifies activities and their costs, then uses drivers to assign costs to cost objects.

data.q: Plant depreciation is generally associated with a facility-level activity.
data.explanation: Plant-wide depreciation supports the facility rather than a particular unit or batch.

data.q: A decrease in selling price, with other factors unchanged, normally increases the break-even point.
data.explanation: Lower selling price reduces contribution per unit, requiring more units to cover fixed cost.

data.q: If actual sales are ₹3,00,000 and break-even sales are ₹4,50,000, the business has no positive margin of safety.
data.explanation: Margin of safety is actual sales minus break-even sales; here the result is negative, so there is no positive safety margin.

data.q: Absorption costing includes fixed manufacturing overhead in inventory cost.
data.explanation: Absorption costing absorbs manufacturing overhead, including fixed production overhead, into product cost.

data.q: The margin of safety is the excess of actual or budgeted sales over break-even sales.
data.explanation: MOS measures the sales cushion before losses begin.

data.q: In marginal costing, fixed cost is generally treated as a period cost rather than a product cost.
data.explanation: Marginal costing separates variable product cost from fixed period cost.

data.q: A cash flow timing difference can make cash available different from accounting profit.
data.explanation: Accrual accounting profit and cash movements occur at different times.

data.q: Budgetary control compares actual performance with budgeted performance and investigates deviations.
data.explanation: Budgetary control uses budgets as benchmarks for monitoring and corrective action.

data.q: Variable overhead efficiency variance is concerned with the difference arising from actual versus standard hours for actual output.
data.explanation: Efficiency variance reflects the effect of using more or fewer hours than the standard allowed.

data.q: A production budget is expressed primarily in units to be produced.
data.explanation: Production planning determines required units after considering sales and inventory.

data.q: A divisional manager who controls revenues and costs is typically responsible for a profit centre.
data.explanation: Profit-centre managers are accountable for both revenues and costs within their area.

data.q: Under the minimax regret approach, the decision maker chooses the alternative with the minimum of the maximum regrets.
data.explanation: Minimax regret seeks to minimise the worst possible opportunity loss.

data.q: A favourable variance is not automatically proof of superior performance; its cause and sustainability should be investigated.
data.explanation: Variance interpretation requires investigation of causes, controllability and operating context.
